before.description: Analyzes capitalist development through changing social relations and class conflict. His historical synthesis becomes an organizing reference for collective Marxist debates about the transition from feudalism.

after.label: Maurice Dobb
after.description: Explains capitalist development through changing production relations and class conflict, while allowing trade to interact with those relations. His historical synthesis prompts international debate over feudalism, labour, the state and accumulation.

after.scope_note: Studies (1946) and the 1950 reply to Sweezy are distinct texts. The reply explicitly uses Marx, Tawney and other historians; it concedes weak evidence for one accumulation hypothesis. Sweezy challenges definition and regional transfer; Takahashi adds a Japanese intervention focused on Western Europe. The primary reply is read in full, not the monograph or all later comparisons. His Asia and historical-stage claims remain attributed positions.

after.label: Rodney Hilton
